t: For necessary expenses of the Office of the Solicitor, $16,313,000.

fable.w: This section is a bare appropriation of funds for a federal office's expenses. There is no tempting reading here: it mentions no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision.
fable.s: For necessary expenses of the Office of the Solicitor, $16,313,000.

opus.w: This section only sets aside money for the Office of the Solicitor's necessary expenses. It does not involve any outside party in a federal decision. The Solicitor's legal role does not count as participation, because there is no consultation, hearing, rulemaking or grant of a right to sue.
opus.b: This is a plain appropriation that sets funding for the Office of the Solicitor. One might be tempted to read the Solicitor as a legal office that handles litigation, but nothing in the text brings in anyone outside the federal government, and there is no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking or right to sue.
